title: Sourcing
info: True break-even cost per output unit, with inputs either bought at market or drawn from another plan's stored snapshot.
unsaved_plan: Save the plan first, sourcing snapshots are stored per plan uuid.
read_only: This plan is read-only, sourcing configuration can't be changed.

controls.cadence_tooltip: Days between two deliveries this plan accepts, per cargo class: production in and out, workforce consumables, repair materials. Empty follows the account default — the placeholder shows what applies. Any positive day count is allowed; 365 means once a year. The cap binds the shipping: a hold needing longer to fill flies partly loaded, and a partial trip pays a full trip.
controls.recompute_chain_tooltip: Recomputes the snapshots of this plan's whole sourcing chain — its sources, this plan and everything drawing from it — upstream first.
controls.import_placeholder: Paste a previously exported sourcing payload

snapshot.stale_sources: {count} upstream snapshot(s) used here are stale
snapshot.base_fraction_tooltip: Base permits this product chain occupies: the plan's own base plus, per source plan, the cost-weighted share of that source's output drawn here, times the source's own base fraction. Fully using this base and half of another one gives 1.50. High values mean the chain ties up several bases — often cheaper to buy than to build.
snapshot.shipping_fraction_tooltip: Ship time this plan's own route pairs occupy: trips per day times round-trip time, divided by a full day of the ships available on the profile. 100 % means one ship flies for this plan around the clock, and a figure past it — shown in red — means the lanes need more ships. Lanes flown by a hired LM carrier count as 0 %.
snapshot.shipping_fraction_link_hint: Click to manage the fleet and its routes.

inputs.lm_buy_tooltip: LM Buy prices this input at an ad on the local market of this base's own planet: nothing is bought at the exchange and no freight is charged for it, whatever cargo class it belongs to. Pick a basis and a price — Manual is the absolute ȼ/unit you offer, any market basis follows that price at the exchange named next to the basis minus the offset you enter (negative bids above it), never dropping below zero. A basis whose side of the book is empty — every side of the synthetic UNIVERSE exchange is — falls back to the 30 day VWAP. The resolved ȼ/unit is shown after the field and turns red once the offset has eaten the whole basis price. Trading on the local market needs a Pro license in game; a Basic account can still trade when the counterpart holds one.
inputs.empty: This plan has no net inputs.

groups.shipFuel: Ship Fuel (already in the shipping cost)

shipping_page.info: Fleet, routes and depots of the whole account. Everything here is account-global; the per-plan pieces — sources, local market rates and the plan CX anchor — stay on each plan's Sourcing tool.
shipping_page.recompute_tooltip: Re-costs every chain from the stored snapshot flows. To refresh the snapshots themselves, use the sourcing tool of a plan.

base_transport.title: Transport for this base
base_transport.info: Every stored lane and chain touching this base, with the figures the account Shipping page shows. Read-only: assignments and rates are edited there.
base_transport.empty: No stored transport touches this base yet — compute a snapshot first, chains are managed on the Shipping page.
base_transport.no_lanes: No stored lanes touch this base.
base_transport.no_chains: No stored chains touch this base.

shipping.title: Shipping
shipping.disabled_info: Shipping is off: freight costs nothing and no snapshot changes. Turning it on marks every stored snapshot stale — the fleet is account-global, so it moves the numbers of every plan.
shipping.cadence_tooltip: Account default for the maximum days between two deliveries of that cargo class. Repair materials follow each plan's own repair day. Every plan may override all three. The cap binds the shipping, not the storage: a hold needing longer to fill flies partly loaded, and a partial trip pays a full trip.
shipping.calibration_info: Calibration constants per hull and FTL reactor, pre-filled from recorded test flights. Cost per parsec and per sublight block are left empty on purpose: an empty field follows the profile's fuel burn at the current FF and SF price. Type a number to override one, empty it again to go back to the derived value. Edited profiles override the preset until reset.
shipping.derived_tooltip: Empty: derived from this profile's fuel burn times the current FF (per parsec) or SF (per sublight block) price. Any number you enter — zero included — wins.
shipping.stl_only_tooltip: A hull built without an FTL drive and reactor — roughly a quarter cheaper. It can only leave its system through a GATE, which drops it straight into the destination orbit, so it serves same-system lanes and lanes whose every inter-system hop is a gate. A lane without such a route is an error, not a slower route: the ship cannot fly it. The FTL constants are greyed out for such a profile and kept as they are.

lm.title: Hired Transport
lm.info: Enter the ȼ per trip an LM transport ad asks for a lane and compare it against flying it yourself. A hired lane pays the entered rate instead of the own fleet cost and drops out of the shipping fraction — the rate covers the whole lane, all of its legs. A lane is flown as one leg per cargo class riding it, each on its own cadence, so days per visit is listed per class. ȼ/u figures are lane averages over everything moving on it, in both directions.
lm.own_per_trip_tooltip: Trip-weighted mean over this lane's {legs} leg(s), which may fly different hulls: the lane costs {daily} ȼ/day in total at {trips} trips/day, ȼ/day being the sum of each leg's trips times that leg's ȼ/trip. Days per visit of each leg are in the Days / Visit column.
lm.empty: This plan owns no route pairs yet — compute a snapshot, or check that its inputs and outputs actually move.

outputs.lm_sell_tooltip: LM Sell puts all of this ticker's market-bound excess on the local market of this base's own planet instead of shipping it to the exchange — the whole ticker is then valued at the ad price. Units other bases draw from here are unaffected and keep shipping on their usual lanes. Pick a basis and a price — Manual is the absolute ȼ/unit you ask, any market basis follows that price at the exchange named next to the basis minus the offset you enter (negative asks above it), never dropping below zero. A basis whose side of the book is empty — every side of the synthetic UNIVERSE exchange is — falls back to the 30 day VWAP. The resolved ȼ/unit is shown after the field and turns red once the offset has eaten the whole basis price. Trading on the local market needs a Pro license in game; a Basic account can still trade when the counterpart holds one.
outputs.empty: This plan has no net outputs.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.info: Ships you own, per type. A ship type is a cargo bay times an FTL reactor — the bay codes are in-game part designations and can't be renamed; the editable label is the blueprint design name. Shipping capacity is the percentage of a type's daily flight time the lanes and chains assigned to it claim: 100% is one hull flying around the clock, and a figure past it — shown in red — means more ships or a bigger hull, it never blocks anything. The table lists only the types you added here — work assigned to a hull you don't own shows up as an advisory instead — and a type you added but set to zero hulls shows no percentage at all. Counts are account-global and stay editable on a read-only plan.
fleet.empty: No ships in the fleet yet — add a type below, then assign lanes and chains to it.

spillover.info: Overflow past 100% is notionally moved onto your types with spare capacity and shown as an amber segment on their bars: the work fits in the fleet overall, just on the wrong hulls. An over-booked type then draws a full bar and prints what's left after spilling — red only when the fleet as a whole is short. This is a reading, not a re-assignment, and it's approximate: minutes move 1:1 between types, but the same work costs different minutes on a different hull.

advisories.title: Fleet Advice
advisories.row: {suggested}: {assignments} assignment(s) now on {current}, every {visit} d → {suggestedVisit} d.

calibration.title: Ship Calibration
calibration.info: Two flights between two known planets — one empty, one loaded — are enough to solve this ship type's constants. You don't have to actually fly them: the in-game BLUEPRINT TEST FLIGHT simulator reports duration, STL fuel, FTL fuel and damage for any path and load.
calibration.blueprint_info: Optional, from the BLUEPRINT panel's Performance block. They seed the profile before any flight: the FTL speed sets minutes per parsec directly, acceleration and empty mass scale the sublight block times, and the engine's fuel rate turns those minutes into fuel. A test flight overrides whatever it can measure; anything you type into the calibration table afterwards wins over both.
calibration.flights_info: Both flights should use the same planet pair. Enter cargo in tonnes, duration in minutes, fuel in units and damage in percent exactly as the game reports them.

warnings.unresolved_route: One flight's planet pair couldn't be found on the map — check the natural ids. That flight constrains nothing.
warnings.same_system_route: A flight that never leaves its system has no parsecs to solve a jump speed from. Pick a pair in two different systems.
warnings.not_solvable: Neither flight was usable, so nothing was solved: the values below are the seed, not a measurement.
warnings.charge_minutes_seeded: Charge time stays at its reactor seed — two flights cannot separate it from the jump speed.
warnings.stl_block_minutes_empty_seeded: The empty sublight block stays seeded (from the blueprint if you entered its stats, otherwise from the nearest reference ship): one of the four time constants has to be, or the system is underdetermined.
warnings.damage_per_stl_block_seeded: Sublight block damage stays seeded from the meteoroid-density law: each flight flies exactly one block, so the block and the jump term cannot be told apart. The jump damage below is what is left over.
warnings.damage_below_block_seed: A flight took less damage than its sublight block alone should cost, so jump damage was floored at zero. The path's meteoroid density is probably lower than the reference.
warnings.loaded_flight_empty: The "loaded" flight carries no cargo, so the loaded block time couldn't be scaled. Enter its cargo tonnage.
warnings.cargo_exceeds_hull: A flight carries more than the hull holds — the load factor was clamped to a full hold.
warnings.negative_solved_time: A solved time came out negative: the entered durations contradict the model, most likely a typo.
warnings.unknown_density: No meteoroid density is known for that path, so the damage rate is not density-normalized.

chains.title: Chains
chains.info: A chain is an ordered LOOP of stops flown by one ship: it claims every flow whose both endpoints are stops of it, and the fullest leg — the weakest link — sets how often the whole loop runs. Chains are account-global; their numbers come from the stored snapshots of their member plans and refresh on a chain recomputation.
chains.name: Name
chains.stops_info: Ordered, closing back to the first stop. Direction matters, repeats are allowed (an out-and-back path is A → B → C → B). An ordered stop pair may belong to only ONE chain.
chains.blocked_stops: Not offered here, another chain already reaches these stops: {stops}
chains.conflict: Chain '{chain}' already reaches both {from} and {to}; two chains may share at most one stop.
chains.empty: No chains yet. Author one when a single ship should serve several planets in one loop instead of flying each lane on its own.

detail.fuel_overridden: This ship profile carries a manual ȼ/parsec or ȼ/STL block, which wins over its fuel burn — so this is the cost basis the ȼ/trip next to it is charged from, not a measured burn.
detail.split_comparison: CX split at {cx} (detour {detour} pc): unsplit {unsplit} ȼ/day vs split {splitCost} ȼ/day — {applied}.
detail.applied_split: the split is what these numbers use
detail.applied_unsplit: the authored loop is what these numbers use
detail.reversed: Flown backwards this loop costs {reversed} ȼ/day against {forward} ȼ/day as authored.
detail.reversed_cheaper: The reversed direction is cheaper — check the stop order.
detail.drop_chip: {stop} at {utilization}% — dropping it onto its own run saves {saving} ȼ/day
detail.storage_warning: {stop}: the chain visits every {visit} d but its storage fills in {fill} d.

auto_chains.title: Automatic Chains
auto_chains.info: Loops nobody authored: one per cargo class per exchange region, CX → base → … → CX, at most five stops in the cheapest order the cargo allows — a base is always visited before the base it feeds, so one lap really delivers. Stops that would only fit by doubling back cost more than their detour budget and stay with the exchange hub/spoke. They are rebuilt on every chain recomputation from the flows the authored chains left, so they cannot be edited — widen a detour budget, pin a ship type, or author a chain of your own instead.
auto_chains.cap_days_tooltip: Longest gap between two visits this loop accepts, the tightest cadence of the bases it serves. A loop reaching the cap flies before its hold is full, and that partial trip pays a full trip.
auto_chains.empty: No automatic chains. Bases carrying less than the stop share, sitting outside the detour budget or anchored at another exchange trade through the exchange instead.

config.min_share_tooltip: Share of a shipments weight OR volume a base has to carry before a loop stops there. Below it the cargo goes through the exchange.
config.detour_tooltip: Parsecs a stop may add to the round trip. The in/out class flies every two weeks and pays every parsec often, the 30 and 90 day classes can afford a short extra jump.

hub_spoke.title: Exchange Hub/Spoke
hub_spoke.info: Cargo of THIS base no chain hauls: it buys what it needs at its exchange and sells its excess at the same one. One row per resource, optionally split by the base pair it moves between; the share is of this base's exchange cargo.
hub_spoke.info_account: Cargo no chain hauls, account wide: the consumer buys it at its exchange and the producer sells its excess at its own. One row per resource, optionally split by the base pair it moves between; the share is of everything rerouted through the exchanges.
hub_spoke.empty: Nothing of this base goes through the exchange: every plan to plan flow it touches rides a chain.
hub_spoke.empty_account: Nothing goes through the exchange: every plan to plan flow rides a chain.

cx_anchor.label: CX Anchor
cx_anchor.tooltip: Exchange a base ships through. Bases sharing an anchor form the region an automatic chain is built over; a plan may override the account wide setting.

depots.title: Depots
depots.info: Planets you hand cargo over at. A depot anchors ROUTING and nothing else: a chain passing close to one may be cut there exactly as it is cut at an exchange, so a gate-side ship and an FTL hauler meet at the depot instead of both flying to the exchange. Each half of such a split can be flown by its own ship type — set them in the chain editor. A depot is not a market: nothing is priced, sourced or sold there, and keeping the warehouse stocked stays your problem. Depots are account-global and can be added for planets no plan of yours sits on.
depots.empty: No depots yet. Mark a gate hub or a warehouse planet as one when two ships should meet there instead of flying to the exchange.

rollup.rent_tooltip: Warehouse rent of every depot a chain calls at, weekly rent divided by seven. Charged ONCE per depot and day however many chains visit it — it is the warehouse standing there, not a docking fee.
